definitions.type: family of elements of the universal enveloping algebra U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: X_r=x^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with X_0=1. U(L) is the complex associative enveloping algebra of L. Elements of U(L) act on V through the extension of act. Juxtaposition such as xv denotes this action.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: Y_r=y^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with Y_0=1, acting on V via act.
U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra of U(L) generated by X_r and Y_r for every integer r>=0.
n=lambda+1.
I={i in Z: 0<=i<=lambda}; its cardinality is n when lambda>=0.

definitions.type: family of vectors of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v for integers i>=0; only indices in I are used for the candidate basis.

definitions.type: subring of Q and hence of C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q: a,b are integers and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are those of Q. All R-actions on submodules of V or C below use this inclusion.
M_R=R tensor_Z M, with scalar multiplication on the R factor.
iota(r tensor m)=r m in V, extended by the balanced tensor universal property. The R-module structure of V is restriction of complex scalars.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I times I
definitions.definition: For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique linear operator sending e_j to e_i and sending e_k to 0 for every k in I with k!=j. The basis existence in N001 makes this definition legitimate.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i in I, J_i={c in C: c e_i belongs to iota(M_R)}.
J=J_0={c in C: c e_0 belongs to iota(M_R)}. This formula defines J also before proving that all J_i agree.
V_K=V(K)=M tensor_Z K, with K acting on the K factor.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh) tensor_Z K, with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h. These integral bracket formulas define the Chevalley construction including in characteristic 2.

propositions.statement: For every semiring A satisfying the strong rank condition, every finite index type T, and every family B_t of additive commutative monoids with A-module structures that are free and finitely generated, finrank_A (product over t in T of B_t)=sum over t in T of finrank_A B_t. Here finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (Cardinal.toNat); the strong rank condition means an injective A-linear map A^a to A^b for finite natural a,b implies a<=b.

propositions.statement: For every semiring A and commutative semiring B both satisfying the strong rank condition, every additive commutative monoid T equipped with a free B-module structure, and every B-algebra structure on A, finrank_A (A tensor_B T)=finrank_B T. Here finrank means Cardinal.toNat of module rank, with no finite-generation assumption; the strong rank condition means injectivity of a linear map from a finite free module of rank a to one of rank b implies a<=b.

propositions.statement: n=lambda+1>0 and I has n elements. The vectors (e_i)_{i in I} form a complex basis of V. For all natural t, hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v, and for t>=1, xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v. All y^t v with t>=lambda+1 vanish. The generator matrices are xe_0=0; xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda; ye_lambda=0; he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I. For every natural r and i in I, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r<=i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these coefficients are integers.

M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restrictions satisfy the stated Chevalley bracket relations. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Every X_r,Y_r preserves iota(M_R). For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). In particular Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), and E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

All J_i for i in I equal J. J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C. Under iota, M_R identifies with the internal direct sum of J e_i over i in I; Q tensor_R J has rational dimension one and its multiplication map into C is injective. There exists a complex scalar b!=0 such that b belongs to J, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} is an R-basis of iota(M_R), equivalently its inverse images form an R-basis of M_R.
propositions.origin: problem.md:118-148; common coordinate module, rank and principality

propositions.statement: There exists a K-basis beta=(beta_i)_{i in I} of V_K, so dim_K V_K=n=lambda+1>0. It has generator matrices x_K beta_0=0; x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<lambda; y_K beta_lambda=0; h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i. There are K-linear endomorphisms T_ij of V_K for i,j in I with T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and zero otherwise, and T_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. Here integer coefficients are mapped into K, every binom(lambda,j) is nonzero in K, and X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for 0<=r<=lambda. The natural K-linear isomorphisms V_K -> M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K intertwine these induced lattice operators; the first sends m tensor c to (1 tensor m) tensor c and its inverse sends (s tensor m) tensor c to m tensor (bar(s)c), where bar:R->K is the extension of the integer map. The second sends u tensor c to (u mod pM_R) tensor c.

argument.text: The representation carries brackets to operator commutators. H005 and H006 therefore give the following inductions. The h identity starts at hv=lambda v, and h y^(t+1)v=y h y^t v-2y^(t+1)v=(lambda-2(t+1))y^(t+1)v. For x the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=lambda v. The step for t>=1 is xy^(t+1)v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+(lambda-2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. The temporary induction hypotheses for these two steps are discharged by natural induction. Thus F001 holds for all natural t, with the x formula used only for t>=1.

produces.statement: For all natural t, hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v; for every t>=1, xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v.

argument.text: H003 gives lambda>=0, so |I|=lambda+1=n>0. Iterating F001, for i in I, x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v!=0: when i=0 the product is 1; otherwise all i factors of the descending product are positive integers and v!=0 by H006. Thus e_i!=0. To prove independence fix any coefficient family c indexed by I and temporarily assume L3: sum_(i in I)c_i e_i=0. For any j in I, apply product_(k in I,k!=j)(h-(lambda-2k)Id_V). The h formula of F001 kills every summand except j; its multiplier on e_j is product_(k!=j)2(k-j), nonzero over C. Hence c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary all coefficients vanish; discharge L3. H004 gives dim_C V=n, so the n independent vectors e_i form a basis.

produces.statement: n>0, |I|=n, and (e_i)_(i in I) is a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Set z=y^(lambda+1)v. By F001, hz=(-lambda-2)z. Expand z in the basis F002; none of the eigenvalues lambda-2i for i in I equals -lambda-2. Applying h-(-lambda-2)Id to this expansion and using independence makes every coefficient zero, so z=0. Every higher lowering power vanishes. Dividing the identities in F001 by i! now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for i>=1 in I, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<lambda, ye_lambda=0 and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i.

produces.statement: y^t v=0 for all t>=lambda+1. On (e_i)_(i in I), xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for i>=1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i.

argument.text: Iterate F003 r times and divide by r!. If r<=i, the x coefficient is (lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)/r!=binom(lambda-i+r,r). If i+r<=lambda, the y coefficient is (i+1)...(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). If r>i the x string reaches xe_0=0, and if i+r>lambda the y string reaches ye_lambda=0. These are integer binomial coefficients, including r=0 where each empty product is 1. Together with F001-F003 these give every clause of N001.

argument.text: By H007, every X_r,Y_r preserves M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; H005 gives h=xy-yx as operators on V, so h also preserves M. Their restrictions satisfy the same commutator identities. H001 makes R the subring obtained by inverting integers prime to p. H007 supplies an integer basis of M that is a complex basis of V; N001 gives complex dimension n and |I|=n, so that basis has n elements and can be indexed by I.

produces.statement: There exists an integer basis a=(a_i)_(i in I) of M which is also a complex basis of V. All X_r,Y_r, x,y,h preserve M and the restricted generators satisfy the Chevalley relations.

binders.type: family of vectors of M indexed by I

argument.text: Choose such a basis a from F001. Its tensor images 1 tensor a_i form an R-basis of M_R: the integer coordinate maps of a tensor to mutually inverse maps between M_R and R^I, sending sum_(i in I) d_i tensor a_i to (d_i)_(i in I). Under iota this basis maps to a_i. If a finite R-linear combination maps to zero, its coefficients vanish by complex independence of a. Hence iota is injective, its image is the R-span of a, and M_R is free of rank n. The image complex-linearly spans V because a is a complex basis. Each X_r,Y_r is complex-linear and preserves M by F001, so preserves this R-span.

produces.statement: iota is injective; M_R is free over R of rank n, iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V, and all X_r,Y_r preserve iota(M_R).

argument.text: Fix i,j in I. The basis formulas in N001 give Q=Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda): X_lambda kills e_k for k<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, which Y_lambda sends back to e_lambda. They also give X_(lambda-i)Q=E_(i,lambda), since the surviving coefficient is binom(lambda-i,lambda-i)=1. Finally Q Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j). Indeed an input e_k with k<j goes below e_lambda and is killed by Q; for k>j it goes past the lowering string and vanishes; and e_j maps with coefficient binom(lambda,lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j). These statements include lambda=0. By H001 and H003, lambda!, j!, (lambda-j)! have no prime factor p. The factorial identity lambda!=binom(lambda,j)j!(lambda-j)! then shows p does not divide binom(lambda,j), so its rational inverse lies in R.

produces.statement: For all i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R and Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

argument.text: Composing the three identities in F003 and using the defining action of matrix units gives E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) for every i,j in I. All factors preserve iota(M_R) by F002, and the scalar is in R by F003, hence every E_ij preserves it. F001-F003 and this formula establish N002. No weights modulo p were separated.

applications.bindings: Set A=Q, B=R and T=M_R, with the inclusion R->Q as algebra map.
hypothesis_checks: Q is a semiring and R is a commutative subring of Q by H001 and D007.
Q is a field; R is a domain with fraction field Q. Clearing denominators and the vector-space dimension inequality establish the strong rank condition for R and Q as explained in S003.
M_R=R tensor_Z M is an additive commutative group with its R-module structure (D008).
N002 states that M_R is free over R of rank n.
The inclusion R->Q makes Q an R-algebra.

applications.bindings: Set A=Q, the finite index type T of the source equal to I, and every source module B_t equal to the local Q-vector space T=Q tensor_R J.
hypothesis_checks: Q is a field and satisfies the strong rank condition by the finite-dimensional injectivity inequality used in S003.
N001 states that I has exactly n elements.
The local T is a Q-vector space by its tensor definition, hence an additive commutative group with Q-module structure.
F002 establishes finite dimensionality; selecting a maximal independent subset of a finite spanning list gives a basis of T, so every constant-family component is free.
F002 gives a finite spanning list of T from a finite generating list of J, hence every component is finitely generated.

argument.text: By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

produces.statement: All J_i equal the nonzero finitely generated R-submodule J of C, and iota identifies M_R with the direct sum of J e_i over i in I.

argument.text: Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

produces.statement: T=Q tensor_R J is finite dimensional over Q; mu:T->C, q tensor c |-> qc, is injective; and Q tensor_R M_R is Q-linearly isomorphic to the finite product T^I.

argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

produces.statement: dim_Q(Q tensor_R J)=1, mu is injective, and the Q-linear span of J in C is one-dimensional.

argument.text: F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

produces.statement: There exist a nonzero a in J, a positive integer k, nonzero rational scalars q_j, integers eta_j and units u_j of R for 1<=j<=k such that q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j and the vectors q_j a generate J over R.

argument.text: Choose a,k,q,eta,u with the properties in F004. Define nu=min_(1<=j<=k) eta_j and b=p^nu a. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j-nu)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j-nu>=0. An index attaining the minimum has q_j a=u_j b, and u_j is an R-unit, so b lies in J and this one generator generates Rb. Thus J=Rb, and b!=0 since p is a nonzero integer and a!=0. F001 now gives iota(M_R)=direct_sum_(i in I)Rb e_i. The vectors b e_i are independent by N001 and b!=0 and span by that equality, so form an R-basis. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. The witnesses are existentially closed to give N003, together with F001-F003.

Fix an arbitrary integer r with 0<=r<=lambda for the quantified factorial formulas.

argument.text: By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Define Phi:V_K->M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c; define its inverse on pure tensors by (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor (bar(s)c). The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

produces.statement: bar:R->K is the extension of the integer map. Phi:V_K -> M_R tensor_R K and Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K are K-linear isomorphisms with the pure-tensor formulas and inverses just given; they intertwine all induced lattice operators.

argument.text: Choose b from N003, so b!=0 and the vectors b e_i form an R-basis of iota(M_R). Define a_i=iota^(-1)(b e_i) in M_R and beta_i=Phi^(-1)(a_i tensor 1) in V_K. The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

produces.statement: beta=(beta_i)_(i in I) is a K-basis of V_K obtained from the R-basis a_i=iota^(-1)(b e_i), with b!=0. In particular dim_K V_K=n=lambda+1>0.

argument.text: The matrices in N001 on e_i are unchanged on b e_i, because all the operators are complex-linear. They therefore are the matrices on a_i over R and on beta_i after applying bar. In particular the formulas for x_K,y_K,h_K in N004 follow with coefficients reduced into K. N002 shows that E_ij preserves iota(M_R). Define T_ij by its induced action after pulling back through iota and then extending scalars using Phi. It sends beta_k to beta_i if k=j and zero otherwise. The full identity in N002 transports to T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1) X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. The scalar bar(binom(lambda,j)) is nonzero, since binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R by N002 and a unital homomorphism to a field sends a unit to a unit.

produces.statement: For all i,j in I, T_ij beta_k equals beta_i when k=j and zero otherwise. Also T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1)X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K, where the displayed binomial coefficient has nonzero image in K. The generator matrices on beta are exactly the reduced generator matrices on e in N001.

argument.text: For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! X_r^K=x_K^r on V_K. Division yields X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, and the identical argument gives Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. F001-F003 and these formulas prove every clause of N004, existentially closing b,a,beta,T. When lambda=0, all factorials and binomial coefficients here are 1. No assumption on algebraic closure of K has been used.

argument.text: Use H001-H002 for the prime-field/scalar identifications and H005 for the Chevalley construction. N001 and N002 supply the basis-defined matrix units and the restrictions of the lattice operators used in this construction, so all definitions of rho,x_K,y_K,h_K,X_K,Y_K are guarded by established inputs. Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

produces.statement: V_K is nonzero, and beta,T satisfy the basis, matrix-unit and factorial formulas of N004.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for every 0<=r<=lambda. Every index lambda-i, lambda and lambda-j in the formula for T_ij lies in this interval, and binom(lambda,j) is nonzero in K. Stability under composition and scalar multiplication now shows that W is invariant under every T_ij.

produces.statement: For every i,j in I, T_ij(W) is contained in W.

argument.text: Split into the exhaustive cases W={0} and W!={0}. The first already yields the desired disjunction. In the nonzero branch temporarily assume L2: W!={0}. Since beta is a basis from N004, there exist w in W, a coefficient family c in K^I, and j in I such that w!=0, w=sum_(i in I)c_i beta_i, and c_j!=0; otherwise all coefficients of every w in W would be zero. Retain this existence as F003 for the next paragraph.

original_context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime.
The field K has characteristic p.
0 <= lambda < p.
With the representation act, V=V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda and has complex dimension lambda+1.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.

M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. M is arbitrary and is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

original_context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

The step for t>=1 is xy^(t+1)v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+(lambda-2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. In the h step L1 is the temporary hypothesis hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

produces.statement: bar:R->K extends the integer map. Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K is the K-linear isomorphism u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c, with inverse [u] tensor c |-> u tensor c. These isomorphisms intertwine rho and X_K,Y_K.

The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

argument.text: N001 gives the explicit generator and divided-power actions on e. Complex linearity gives the same coefficients on b e_i, hence on a_i via iota and on beta_i after applying bar. Consequently x_K beta_0=0, x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda, y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda, y_K beta_lambda=0, and h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i for i in I. N002 gives preservation of iota(M_R) by E_ij. Define T_ij by the induced lattice action after pulling back through iota and extending scalars using Phi; then T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and 0 otherwise. Transporting the equality E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) from N002 gives T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1)X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. argument.text: For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! X_r^K=x_K^r on V_K. Division yields X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, and the identical argument gives Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. argument.text: The representation carries brackets to operator commutators. H005 and H006 therefore give the following inductions. In the x step for t>=1, L2 is the temporary hypothesis xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v; its use of the h identity is justified by the completed first induction. argument.text: By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

argument.text: Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

argument.text: F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

argument.text: By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. original_context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime.
The field K has characteristic p.
0 <= lambda < p.
With the representation act, V=V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda and has complex dimension lambda+1.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.

M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. M is arbitrary and is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

original_context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

argument.text: The representation carries brackets to operator commutators. H005 and H006 therefore give the following inductions. The step for t>=1 is xy^(t+1)v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+(lambda-2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. In the h step L1 is the temporary hypothesis hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v. In the x step for t>=1, L2 is the temporary hypothesis xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v; its use of the h identity is justified by the completed first induction. Thus e_i!=0. To prove independence fix any coefficient family c indexed by I and temporarily assume L3: sum_(i in I)c_i e_i=0. For any j in I, apply product_(k in I,k!=j)(h-(lambda-2k)Id_V). The h formula of F001 kills every summand except j; its multiplier on e_j is product_(k!=j)2(k-j), nonzero over C. Hence c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary all coefficients vanish; discharge L3. H004 gives dim_C V=n, so the n independent vectors e_i form a basis.

produces.statement: n>0, |I|=n, and the family e indexed by I is a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Set z=y^(lambda+1)v. By F001, hz=(-lambda-2)z. Expand z in the basis F002; none of the eigenvalues lambda-2i for i in I equals -lambda-2. Applying h-(-lambda-2)Id to this expansion and using independence makes every coefficient zero, so z=0. Every higher lowering power vanishes. Dividing the identities in F001 by i! now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for i>=1 in I, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<lambda, ye_lambda=0 and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i.

produces.statement: y^(t0)v=0 for all t0>=lambda+1. On the basis e indexed by I, xe_0=0, xe_(i0)=(lambda-i0+1)e_(i0-1) for i0>=1 in I, ye_(i0)=(i0+1)e_(i0+1) for i0<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_(i0)=(lambda-2i0)e_(i0).

argument.text: Iterate F003 r times and divide by r!. If r<=i, the x coefficient is (lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)/r!=binom(lambda-i+r,r). If i+r<=lambda, the y coefficient is (i+1)...(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). If r>i the x string reaches xe_0=0, and if i+r>lambda the y string reaches ye_lambda=0. These are integer binomial coefficients, including r=0 where each empty product is 1. Together with F001-F003 these give all the asserted basis and operator formulas.

argument.text: By H007, every X_r,Y_r preserves M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; H005 gives h=xy-yx as operators on V, so h also preserves M. argument.text: Choose such a basis a from F001. Its tensor images 1 tensor a_i form an R-basis of M_R: the integer coordinate maps of a tensor to mutually inverse maps between M_R and R^I, sending sum_(i in I) d_i tensor a_i to (d_i)_(i in I). Under iota this basis maps to a_i. If a finite R-linear combination maps to zero, its coefficients vanish by complex independence of a. Hence iota is injective, its image is the R-span of a, and M_R is free of rank n. The image complex-linearly spans V because a is a complex basis. produces.statement: iota is injective; M_R is free over R of rank n, iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V, and all X_r,Y_r preserve iota(M_R).

argument.text: Fix i,j in I. The basis formulas in N001 give Q=Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda): X_lambda kills e_k for k<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, which Y_lambda sends back to e_lambda. argument.text: By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

argument.text: Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

produces.statement: T=Q tensor_R J is finite dimensional over Q; mu:T->C, q tensor c |-> qc, is injective; and Q tensor_R M_R is Q-linearly isomorphic to the finite product T^I.

argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

produces.statement: dim_Q(Q tensor_R J)=1, mu is injective, and the Q-linear span of J in C is one-dimensional.

argument.text: F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

produces.statement: There exist a nonzero a0 in J, a positive integer k0, nonzero rational scalars q0_j0, integers eta0_j0 and units u0_j0 of R for 1<=j0<=k0 such that q0_j0=p^(eta0_j0)u0_j0 and the vectors q0_j0 a0 generate J over R.

argument.text: Choose a,k,q,eta,u with the properties in F004. Define nu=min_(1<=j<=k) eta_j and b=p^nu a. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j-nu)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j-nu>=0. An index attaining the minimum has q_j a=u_j b, and u_j is an R-unit, so b lies in J and this one generator generates Rb. Thus J=Rb, and b!=0 since p is a nonzero integer and a!=0. F001 now gives iota(M_R)=direct_sum_(i in I)Rb e_i. The vectors b e_i are independent by N001 and b!=0 and span by that equality, so form an R-basis. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. Existentially close the witnesses; together with F001-F003 this gives all the asserted coordinate-module and basis properties.

inputs.statement: p is prime.
The field K has characteristic p.
0 <= lambda < p.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.

n=lambda+1>0 and I has n elements. The vectors (e_i)_{i in I} form a complex basis of V. For all natural t, hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v, and for t>=1, xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v. For every natural r and i in I, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r<=i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these coefficients are integers.

M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restricted operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y and xy-yx=h. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Every X_r,Y_r preserves iota(M_R). For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). In particular Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), and E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

All J_i for i in I equal J. J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C. Under iota, M_R identifies with the internal direct sum of J e_i over i in I; Q tensor_R J has rational dimension one and its multiplication map into C is injective. There exists a complex scalar b!=0 such that b belongs to J, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} is an R-basis of iota(M_R), equivalently its inverse images form an R-basis of M_R.

argument.text: By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Define Phi:V_K->M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c; define its inverse on pure tensors by (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor (bar(s)c). The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

produces.statement: bar:R->K extends the integer map. Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K is the K-linear isomorphism u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c, with inverse [u] tensor c |-> u tensor c. These isomorphisms intertwine rho and X_K,Y_K.

argument.text: Choose b from N003, so b!=0 and the vectors b e_i form an R-basis of iota(M_R). Define a_i=iota^(-1)(b e_i) in M_R and beta_i=Phi^(-1)(a_i tensor 1) in V_K. The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

argument.text: N001 gives the explicit generator and divided-power actions on e. Complex linearity gives the same coefficients on b e_i, hence on a_i via iota and on beta_i after applying bar. Consequently x_K beta_0=0, x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda, y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda, y_K beta_lambda=0, and h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i for i in I. N002 gives preservation of iota(M_R) by E_ij. Define T_ij by the induced lattice action after pulling back through iota and extending scalars using Phi; then T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and 0 otherwise. Transporting the equality E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) from N002 gives T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1)X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. This scalar is defined and nonzero, because N002 states that binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R and a unital homomorphism to a field maps units to units.

produces.statement: For all i0,j0,k0 in I, T_(i0,j0) beta_k0 equals beta_i0 when k0=j0 and zero otherwise. Also T_(i0,j0)=bar(binom(lambda,j0))^(-1)X_(lambda-i0)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j0)^K, where the displayed binomial coefficient has nonzero image in K. The generator matrices are x_K beta_0=0, x_K beta_i0=(lambda-i0+1)beta_(i0-1) for 1<=i0<=lambda, y_K beta_i0=(i0+1)beta_(i0+1) for 0<=i0<lambda, y_K beta_lambda=0, and h_K beta_i0=(lambda-2i0)beta_i0 for i0 in I.

argument.text: For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! X_r^K=x_K^r on V_K. Division yields X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, and the identical argument gives Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. F001-F003 and these formulas prove all the asserted basis, scalar-extension and operator properties, existentially closing b,a,beta,T. When lambda=0, all factorials and binomial coefficients here are 1. No assumption on algebraic closure of K has been used.

argument.text: Use H001-H002 for the prime-field/scalar identifications and H005 for the Chevalley construction. N001 and N002 supply the basis-defined matrix units and the restrictions of the lattice operators used in this construction, so all definitions of rho,x_K,y_K,h_K,X_K,Y_K are guarded by established inputs. Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for every 0<=r<=lambda. Every index lambda-i, lambda and lambda-j2 in the formula for T_(i,j2) lies in this interval, and binom(lambda,j2) is nonzero in K. Stability under composition and scalar multiplication now shows that W is invariant under every T_(i,j2), hence under all matrix units since i,j2 were arbitrary.

produces.statement: For every i0,j0 in I, T_(i0,j0)(W) is contained in W.

argument.text: Split into the exhaustive cases W={0} and W!={0}. In the zero branch temporarily assume L3: W={0}; the desired disjunction follows immediately, so discharge L3 to close that branch. In the nonzero branch temporarily assume L2: W!={0}. Since beta is a basis from N004, there exist w in W, a coefficient family c in K^I, and j in I such that w!=0, w=sum_(i in I)c_i beta_i, and c_j!=0; otherwise all coefficients of every w in W would be zero. Retain this existence as F003 for the next paragraph.

produces.statement: There exist w0 in W, c0 in K^I and j0 in I such that w0!=0, w0=sum_(i0 in I)c0_i0 beta_i0, and c0_j0!=0.

argument.text: Choose w,c,j from F003. For every i in I, the matrix-unit action in N004 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. F002 places this vector in W; division by the nonzero c_j in the field K yields beta_i in W. Thus all basis vectors belong to W and W=V_K. Discharge the nonzero-case assumption L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V_K under L1.

produces.statement: W={0} or W=V_K.

argument.text: Discharge L1 to conclude that invariance under x_K,y_K,h_K implies W={0} or W=V_K, and universally quantify the arbitrary subspace W. Combine this with nonzeroness from F001 to obtain the target conclusion. Since the Chevalley generators span L_K, their invariant subspaces are exactly the L_K-submodules. The endpoint lambda=0 uses a single basis vector with all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients equal to 1. By H003, for p=2 the allowed lambda values are 0 and 1, and the same formulas apply. No step separates h_K-eigenvalues or assumes K algebraically closed.

H001-H007 retain primality, characteristic, the full range, characteristic-zero irreducible highest-weight module with dimension, all three Chevalley commutators, the nonzero highest vector with both equations, and the arbitrary admissible lattice with its simultaneous integer/complex basis and all divided-power stability. All seven original H occur in the graph and are used; the characteristic-zero irreducibility/highest-weight description in H004 is retained although the proof needs only its dimension in addition to H005-H006. D001-D003 preserve X_r=x^r/r!, Y_r=y^r/r! and the generated unital integer algebra. D004-D006 preserve n and the candidate basis; defining the same e_i formula for all natural i is a harmless extension of notation, and all basis indices remain exactly 0..lambda. D007 uses H001 to define the genuine subring Z_(p). D008 is the abstract tensor module, and D009 is its multiplication map; injectivity is proved in R002/S002 rather than assumed by their types. D010 is guarded by N001, so no matrix unit precedes the proved complex basis. D011-D012 are preimages of an R-submodule under multiplication by e_i, hence legitimate R-submodules; J is defined by the zeroth coordinate and equality of all coordinates is proved in R003/S001. D013 is the original tensor V(K), D014 uses H005 for the Chevalley Lie lattice, and D015-D020 require N002 for lattice preservation before defining reduced actions; all use sites supply those guards directly. D021 uses H001-H002 for the prime field and its embedding. Thus none of the D types grants a desired basis, equality of J_i, injectivity, or principality. The two actual native theorem sources M001 and M002 were probed successfully in the pinned library and compared with Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Constructions.lean:297-302 and :345-378. Their restatements preserve all semiring/module structures, strong rank conditions, freeness, finite-index/finite-generation premises where present, and the absence of a finite-generation premise in M002. original_context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime.
The field K has characteristic p.
0 <= lambda < p.
With the representation act, V=V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda and has complex dimension lambda+1.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.

M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. M is arbitrary and is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

original_context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.
